transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

I've been feeling extremely anxious and unsafe lately because I feel like I'm constantly being watched and monitored by other people. This has been going on for about 11 months now, and it's getting really hard to handle.
Have you also had any periods of several days or longer when your mood was unusually high or irritable, or times when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things?

I haven't had any periods where my mood was unusually high, irritable, or extremely depressed. However, I have definitely lost interest in almost everything and don't find pleasure in the things I used to enjoy anymore. It just feels like nothing brings me joy lately.
Have the feelings of being watched happened only when you were feeling depressed and losing interest, or have they continued even when your mood was otherwise normal?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't kept track of whether they always happen at the same time or if they're separate. It all just blends together and has been going on for so long.
Besides feeling watched, have you noticed hearing voices, seeing things others don't, or having trouble with your thoughts or speech becoming hard to follow?

No, I don't hear any strange voices or see things that aren't actually there, and my thoughts and speech feel normal to me. My main issue is just that constant, terrifying feeling of being watched and monitored by people.
In the past 11 months, have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or hopeless most of the day nearly every day, along with changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or guilt?
No, I haven't experienced a period like that at all. I haven't felt depressed or hopeless, and my sleep, appetite, and energy levels have been normal.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent 11-month fixed persecutory belief that others are watching/monitoring them, with marked distress but no hallucinations, disorganized speech/behavior, manic episodes, or clear major depressive episode. This pattern most strongly supports Delusional Disorder; schizophrenia is less likely due to absence of other psychotic symptoms, and major depressive disorder is not supported because they deny a sustained depressive syndrome.
